classification.difficultyReason: Represent the tower and swimmer as a right triangle, transfer the depression angle to the angle of elevation, and rearrange the tangent ratio for horizontal distance.

content.prompt: From a point on top of a tower of height $5.8\text{ m}$, the angle of depression to a swimmer is $16^\circ$. How far from the base of the tower is the swimmer? Give your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a metre.

answer.worked:
Let $x\text{ m}$ be the horizontal distance from the base of the tower to the swimmer. The angle of elevation from the swimmer is $16^\circ$, by alternate angles between parallel horizontal lines.

$$\begin{align*}\tan16^\circ&=\frac{5.8}{x}\\x\tan16^\circ&=5.8\\x&=\frac{5.8}{\tan16^\circ}\\x&\approx20.2\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
